title: MorningJet's new-route fare
prompt: MorningJet is considering a new daily round-trip route between Chicago and Nashville. Management must choose an introductory average fare and determine whether the route can cover its costs in its first full year.
objective: Recommend an average fare for the Chicago-Nashville route and determine whether expected demand makes the route commercially feasible.

clarificationOptions.label: What decision does management need to make?
clarificationOptions.response: Choose the average one-way fare and decide whether to launch the route for a full year.

clarificationOptions.label: How will management define commercial success?
clarificationOptions.response: The route should cover its route-specific fixed and variable costs in year one while retaining a reasonable demand buffer above break-even.

clarificationOptions.label: Is aircraft capacity fixed for the first year?
clarificationOptions.response: Yes. The planned schedule provides 65,000 one-way seats for the year.

clarificationOptions.label: Will the loyalty program change for this route?
clarificationOptions.response: No material loyalty-program changes are planned for the launch.

facts.text: At a $180 average one-way fare, forecast year-one demand is 52,000 passengers.
At a $150 average one-way fare, forecast year-one demand is 62,000 passengers.
At a $220 average one-way fare, forecast year-one demand is 38,000 passengers.
Variable cost is $70 per passenger across the considered fare options.
A $180 fare produces a $110 contribution margin per passenger.
The route requires $4.4 million of annual route-specific fixed cost.
At a $180 fare, the route breaks even at 40,000 annual passengers.
The planned daily schedule provides 65,000 one-way seats annually.
Forecast demand at $180 is 12,000 passengers, or 30%, above break-even demand.
Comparable nonstop fares on similar regional routes average $175 to $195.
A small survey found that some business travelers prefer complimentary lounge access.
At the $180 fare and forecast demand, the route is expected to generate $1.32 million before shared corporate overhead.

investigationNodes.label: Understand route unit economics
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Variable cost is $70 per passenger and annual route-specific fixed cost is $4.4 million. The unit-economics exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Calculate contribution margin at the midpoint fare
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: At $180, each passenger contributes $110 after the $70 variable cost.

investigationNodes.label: Review demand at alternative fares
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Demand declines as the fare rises. The forecast-demand exhibit compares the three tested price points.

investigationNodes.label: Benchmark comparable nonstop fares
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Comparable regional nonstop fares average $175 to $195, so $180 sits within the market range.

investigationNodes.label: Check available seat capacity
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: The proposed schedule supplies 65,000 seats, enough to serve forecast demand at each tested fare.

investigationNodes.label: Explore lounge preferences
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: A small survey shows some interest in lounge access, but it does not materially change the route's demand forecast or economics.

investigationNodes.label: Test commercial feasibility at the midpoint fare
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: At $180, forecast demand is 12,000 passengers above break-even and produces an estimated $1.32 million route contribution. The route appears commercially feasible with a meaningful demand buffer.

insights.label: The $180 fare generates the highest expected route contribution among the tested fares.
The lowest fare creates the highest route contribution because it attracts the most passengers.

exhibits.title: Forecast annual demand by average fare

insights.label: Forecast demand falls as the average fare increases.
Seat capacity prevents MorningJet from serving forecast demand at $180.

calculations.prompt: At a $180 fare, contribution margin is $110 per passenger and annual route-specific fixed cost is $4.4 million. How many annual passengers are required to break even?

decisions.label: Launch at a $180 average fare, monitor booking pace, and preserve the option to adjust within the competitive range.
Launch at $150 to maximize passenger volume.
Launch at $220 to maximize contribution per passenger.

risks.label: Actual demand could fall below the forecast and narrow the break-even buffer.
Competitors may lower fares after MorningJet enters the route.
Fuel or airport costs could raise variable cost above $70 per passenger.

nextSteps.label: Open a limited booking window at $180 and compare early bookings with the demand forecast.
Purchase another aircraft before testing demand.
Build a dedicated lounge before launching the route.

efficientPaths.label: Establish contribution margin, then test demand and feasibility
Establish demand and capacity, then confirm unit economics
